title: Mapping Laws Relevant to Online Violence in Nepal
subtitle: A Human Rights & Case Law Review

headlineFinding: Nepal’s legal framework treats online violence not as a violation of bodily autonomy and human rights, but as a breach of patriarchal 'honor' (ijjat) and 'character' (charitra). Over-reliance on Section 47 of the Electronic Transaction Act criminalizes legitimate speech while leaving survivors without effective protection or compensation.

chapters.title: Introduction, Scope & Research Methodology
chapters.lede: The study analyses the existing legal framework of Nepal concerning online violence, and compares it against three human rights lenses: Freedom of Expression, Right to Privacy, and Freedom from Violence.

chapters.title: Three Human Rights Lenses
chapters.lede: Evaluating domestic legislation against international standards under ICCPR, CEDAW, and the Constitution of Nepal.

chapters.title: 2D Policy Matrix: 32 Provisions across 7 Laws
chapters.lede: Cross-mapping seven key statutes against human rights benchmarks to categorize provisions as rights-protecting, double-edged, or risk-creating.

chapters.title: Eight Systemic Statutory Flaws
chapters.lede: Analyzing structural loopholes including the ETA 47 trap, vague moralistic terms, 90-day filing limits, and forced reconciliation mandates.

chapters.title: 15 Court Case Studies (Judicial Explorer)
chapters.lede: Detailed examination of 15 real judicial cases from District to Appellate Courts.

chapters.title: Seven Policy Recommendations for Legal Reform
chapters.lede: A human rights-centered roadmap for overhauling Nepal's legal response to online gender-based violence.

recommendations.title: Enact a Specialized Online Gender-Based Violence Statute
recommendations.details: Repeal Section 47 of the ETA and replace it with a dedicated law recognizing non-consensual image sharing, cyberstalking, doxxing, and extortion as human rights violations with civil and criminal remedies.

recommendations.title: Eliminate the 90-Day Statute of Limitations
recommendations.details: Amend Section 229 of the Penal Code to abolish or significantly extend the limitation period for reporting sexual harassment and online violence.

recommendations.title: Mandate Fast-Track Content Takedown Orders
recommendations.details: Empower courts and human rights commissions to issue emergency interim injunctions compelling tech platforms and ISPs to remove non-consensual intimate images within 24 hours.
